subject: retry-backoff
seam: crates/engine/src/retry.rs (with_retry_within: stated delay outranks the computed rung, CALL_BUDGET deadline, over-budget terminal state)
crates/engine/src/providers.rs (stated_retry_after: 3 header spellings / 2 unit systems, classified at the boundary)
crates/runner/src/compare.rs (TargetHealth: one breaker per target as a candidate filter, all-open degrades to trying)
seam_notes: The direction said with_retry's CLOSURE signature must widen so the response reaches the scheduler; it does not have to. The response is gone by then, but the CLASS is not: putting the stated delay on EngineError::RateLimited keeps classification at the boundary that holds the structured response and leaves the FnMut() -> Result<T> seam and all 4 call sites untouched. The health filter had to live in compute_cell, not beside it: compare dispatches ONE parallel_map over target x case, so a filter over a pre-computed candidate list has nothing to filter - the verdict is consulted per cell, target-major, and identity is the pre-filter index. Provider-boundary suite is a ~40-line std::net::TcpListener stub, not wiremock/httpmock/mockito: the engine client is BLOCKING reqwest and all three are async, so each would drag a tokio runtime plus a cargo-deny surface into a crate that has neither, to serve one canned response.
falsifier: The retry-after half rests on providers actually stating a delay on 429. This run could not check it - the worktree carries no engine log corpus - so it remains the proposal's own open falsifier: if a week of crates/engine logs shows no Retry-After on any 429 received, the header accept-list is dead code and only the 60s CALL_BUDGET deadline is earning its keep. The filter's falsifier is cheaper: if run history shows errored_cases at zero across every recorded run, the breaker guards a case that has not occurred.
